issues.t: Lower intake manifold gasket leaks coolant
issues.sym: Coolant level drops with no clear leak, a sweet smell after driving, overheating, or milky oil on the dipstick.
issues.why: The original intake gaskets on these GM V6 engines break down with age and coolant, letting coolant leak outside the engine or into the oil.
issues.next: Check coolant and oil often. If the oil looks milky, stop driving and get it fixed, because coolant in the oil can wreck the bearings. Ask for updated gaskets and a coolant flush.

issues.t: Oil leaking onto exhaust manifold can start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: A burning oil smell, smoke from under the hood, especially after hard braking, or oil around the valve covers.
issues.why: Oil seeping from the valve cover area or spilled during an oil change can drip onto the hot exhaust manifold and ignite, then spread to the plastic spark plug wire channel. GM issued several recalls for this.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Have a Buick dealer check your VIN, because there were several separate recalls. Do not overfill the oil, and fix valve cover leaks promptly.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slips or fails
issues.sym: Slipping, flaring between gears, harsh shifts, stuck in one gear, or the car will not move.
issues.why: The four-speed automatic can wear its clutches or suffer valve body and solenoid problems. Owners report failures at a wide range of mileages.
issues.next: Have the fluid and codes checked as soon as shifting changes. A solenoid or valve body repair is far less work than a full rebuild.

issues.t: Car stalls or will not start and dash lights flicker
issues.sym: The car will not start while the dash lights flicker or blink, or the engine cuts out when the turn signal or another control is used.
issues.why: Owners most often trace these faults to a worn ignition switch or its wiring and connections, which can drop power to the engine controls.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Have the ignition switch, battery cables and connections tested. Stalling while driving is a safety risk, so do not put it off.

issues.t: Engine stalls from a failing crankshaft or airflow sensor
issues.sym: The engine shuts off while driving or at a stop and may restart once it cools.
issues.why: A failing crankshaft position sensor or mass airflow sensor sends a bad signal to the engine computer.
issues.next: Stalling in traffic is dangerous, so get it checked soon. Have stored codes read; the crank sensor is a common fix.

issues.t: Key stuck in the ignition from a failed shifter part
issues.sym: The key will not come out of the ignition even though the car is in Park.
issues.why: The shifter interlock that tells the ignition the car is in Park fails, so the key stays locked in.
issues.next: Have the shifter and interlock checked. It is a common repair and usually does not need major parts.

issues.t: Power windows stop working
issues.sym: A window will not go up or down, falls into the door, or makes a grinding noise.
issues.why: The window regulators and switches wear out on this generation.
issues.next: Have the window regulator and switch tested. Tape or prop the glass up if it will not close, to keep rain out.

issues.t: Steering can become very heavy in turns (recall)
issues.sym: Steering suddenly takes much more effort, especially during left turns, like a car without power steering.
issues.why: The pinion shaft in the steering gear can move upward because of a bearing problem.
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. Have a Buick dealer check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Brake line can wear through (recall)
issues.sym: A soft or sinking brake pedal and brake fluid leaking.
issues.why: A brake line can rub and wear through, leaking fluid and possibly losing half the braking system.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Have a Buick dealer check your VIN. If the pedal feels soft, do not drive the car until it is inspected.

issues.t: Engine may not start and could catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: The engine will not start, or there is a fuel smell under the hood.
issues.why: A defect in the fuel and intake system on some 1996 cars could prevent starting and possibly cause an engine compartment fire.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Have a Buick dealer check your VIN for this recall.

issues.t: Windshield wipers can stop working (recall)
issues.sym: The wipers stop working, cutting your view in rain or snow.
issues.why: A defect in the wiper system could stop the wipers.
issues.next: Have a Buick dealer check your VIN for the wiper recall.

issues.t: ABS motor short can cause an underhood fire (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell or smoke from under the hood, sometimes with the ABS light on.
issues.why: A short in the ABS pump motor can overheat a brake pipe and melt a nearby plastic fuel hose.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Have a Buick dealer check your VIN for the recall right away.

issues.t: Seat belt buckle may not hold in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: A seat belt that seems latched may not hold in a crash.
issues.why: Some seat belt buckles may not fully latch.
issues.next: Make sure each buckle clicks firmly, and have a Buick dealer check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Excessive oil consumption (2.4L)
issues.sym: You need to add a quart of oil every 1,000 to 2,000 miles, the low oil light comes on, or the engine smokes or misfires.
issues.why: Piston rings on the 2.4L engine can get stuck with carbon, letting oil burn. GM issued a bulletin to replace the pistons and rings.
issues.next: Check the oil every fill-up. Ask a Buick dealer whether your car qualifies for the oil consumption bulletin or coverage. Running low can destroy the timing chain and engine.

issues.t: Timing chain stretch and rattle
issues.sym: A rattle on cold start, a check engine light with cam and crank timing codes (such as P0016 or P0017), rough running or a loss of power.
issues.why: The timing chain stretches and its guides wear, often made worse by low or old oil.
issues.next: Have it checked as soon as you hear rattling or see timing codes. A chain that jumps can badly damage the engine.

issues.t: Engine stalls or loses power while driving
issues.sym: The engine stumbles, loses power or shuts off while driving, sometimes with a check engine light.
issues.why: Owners link it to timing and camshaft sensor faults, low oil, and related engine problems. It was the most reported 2011 Regal complaint.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Have codes read right away. Check the oil level, since low oil can cause timing problems on these engines.

issues.t: Transmission will not engage
issues.sym: The car will not move in Drive or Reverse, or slips badly.
issues.why: The six-speed automatic can fail internally. Owners report failures around 95,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the fluid level and codes checked. Do not keep driving a transmission that slips.

issues.t: Front seat wiring can short and cause a fire (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell from under a front seat, or seat features that stop working.
issues.why: Wires in the front seat harness can chafe and short circuit.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Have a Buick dealer check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Key can be removed when not in Park (recall)
issues.sym: The key comes out even though the shifter is not in Park, and the car can roll away.
issues.why: The ignition key interlock does not always stop key removal out of Park.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake, and have a Buick dealer check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Front turn signal can be partly dark (recall)
issues.sym: Part of a front turn signal does not light, and the driver gets no warning.
issues.why: The car does not warn the driver when one bulb in the front turn signal is out.
issues.next: Check your turn signals and have a Buick dealer check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: eAssist charging system can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: A burning or melting smell, smoke from the trunk, stalling or a no-start.
issues.why: The eAssist hybrid battery and generator control module can fail and overheat.
issues.next: Stop driving if you smell burning from the trunk. Have a Buick dealer check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Rear toe links can rust and break (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk from the rear, the car wanders, or it pulls badly and feels unstable.
issues.why: The rear toe links can corrode and fracture, which affects control of the car.
issues.next: Have a Buick dealer check your VIN for the toe link recalls.

issues.t: Piston damage from low-speed pre-ignition (2.0L turbo)
issues.sym: A sudden loud knock or bang under hard acceleration at low speed, followed by misfire, a check engine light, or a dead engine.
issues.why: Turbocharged direct-injection engines can suffer low-speed pre-ignition, where fuel ignites too early and can crack a piston. GM issued a bulletin telling shops which oil to use on 2.0L engines to help prevent piston failure.
issues.next: Use the oil type GM specifies for your engine and change it on time. If you hear a heavy knock under acceleration, stop and have it checked before driving further.

issues.t: Power steering assist cuts out with Service Power Steering message
issues.sym: Steering suddenly gets heavy and the dash shows Service Power Steering or Steering Assist Is Reduced.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins for the electric power steering losing assist, linked to grounds, the steering control module software and a fuse that can blow after an improper jump start.
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. Pull over safely and restart the car. Have a Buick dealer check the steering bulletins; the fix is often a ground repair or software update.

issues.t: Hard start or black smoke after sitting
issues.sym: Long cranking before the engine starts, or a puff of black smoke when starting after the car has sat.
issues.why: GM traced this to the fuel delivery on the direct-injection 2.0L turbo and issued bulletins with repair steps.
issues.next: Ask a Buick dealer to check the hard-start bulletins before parts are replaced.

issues.t: Reduced power from a failing high-pressure fuel pump
issues.sym: Check engine light, code P228C, and reduced engine power or hesitation.
issues.why: The engine-driven high-pressure fuel pump on the direct-injection 2.0L turbo can fail to hold pressure. GM issued a bulletin to replace it.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Ask the dealer about the high-pressure fuel pump bulletin.

issues.t: Oil leak at the engine front cover
issues.sym: Oil seeping at the passenger side of the engine, oil spots under the car, or a burning oil smell.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for oil leaks at the timing (front) cover on the 2.0L turbo.
issues.next: Keep the oil topped up and have the leak found. Ask the shop about the front cover bulletin.

issues.t: Brake pedal can stick down
issues.sym: The brake pedal stays down or is slow to come back up after you brake.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin to replace the brake pedal arm for a pedal that sticks.
issues.next: Have the brakes checked right away and ask a dealer about the pedal bulletin.

issues.t: Rear brake caliper pistons can corrode (recall)
issues.sym: Weaker braking or a dragging rear brake.
issues.why: The rear caliper pistons may not have enough protective coating and can corrode.
issues.next: Have a Buick dealer check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Rear seat belts may not hold in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs. The problem shows up only in a crash.
issues.why: The rear outboard seat belts may not restrain passengers properly.
issues.next: Have a Buick dealer check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Power brake assist can be lost (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal becomes hard and the car takes longer to stop.
issues.why: A fault can cause the loss of power brake assist.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Have a Buick dealer check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Hard brake pedal or hissing from oil in the brake booster
issues.sym: A hard brake pedal or a hissing, air-like noise when braking.
issues.why: GM found that engine oil can get into the brake booster vacuum supply and damage the booster.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Have the brakes checked right away. A shop can follow the GM bulletin to replace the booster and fix the cause.

issues.t: Water pump noise or coolant leak
issues.sym: A whine or grinding from the engine, a coolant smell, or a dropping coolant level with a check engine light.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins for water pump noise and for coolant or oil leaks on the 2.0L turbo engine.
issues.next: Watch the coolant level and temperature gauge. Have the pump checked before it leaks badly.

issues.t: Fuel in the oil
issues.sym: A fuel smell from the oil, a rising oil level, or rough running.
issues.why: GM found excess fuel could build up in the oil and issued a bulletin for an oil change, PCV valve and engine computer update.
issues.next: Ask a Buick dealer about the bulletin. Change the oil on time.

issues.t: Sticky or notchy steering feel near center
issues.sym: The steering wheel feels like it sticks then jumps when making small corrections on the highway.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for a stick-slip feel in the electric steering.
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. Ask a Buick dealer to check the steering bulletin.
